correctness.rationale: The strictly positive graph-pinning energy proves SPD. The exact tridiagonal determinant recurrence has degree four. Forty-eight pairwise disjoint rational endpoint sign changes isolate the complete spectra for the twelve matrices. Nine strict rational comparisons between certified upper and lower condition-number bounds prove the three unique global winners. A grounded-principal-minor comparison proves that site 2 uniquely wins for all sufficiently large gains: its grounded minimum is 1, and explicit test vectors show each competing grounded minimum is below 1. Continuity proves two distinct winner changes and robustness under small perturbations. Limits: gain transitions are not isolated exactly.

evidence: Jafarizadeh (2024), Sections IV, VII-E and Remark 14: a weighted path with a single pin is a special case of a general network eigenratio optimization with independently variable link weights and pinning parameters.

broader_coverage.reasoning: These analytical formulations include a comparable spectral objective but optimize design degrees of freedom not allowed here. An optimum with free link weights and gain does not imply fixed-weight site rankings at three different externally set gains; no stated theorem constrains or excludes this return. This comparison expressly does not claim that the general placement problem is new.

Neither inspected account proves an exact two-to-four-to-two return on a fixed weighted four-path at prescribed gains. The exact finite certificate gives an explicit, stronger nonmonotone order pattern.

originality.rationale: The objective and general gain-sensitive pinning optimization already appear in 2015 and 2016 studies; those are expressly not claimed new. Exact fixed-weight four-path winner reentrance (2 at gain 10, 4 at 50, back to 2 at 500 and eventually forever), with a rational reproducible certificate, grounded-matrix asymptotics and perturbation robustness, is not implied by the closest inspected statements, including the later free-weight spectral design theory. Incomplete index and some article coverage leave publication priority risk.
residual_risks: Search and accessible literature are not exhaustive; an unindexed identical four-path example could exist.
The 2015 article was inspected through an author-posted text extraction and publisher metadata, rather than a direct full publisher PDF.
Openly accessible related weighted-network optimization results include much broader variable-weight design, but do not mathematically imply the prescribed fixed-parameter site ranking.

value.rationale: The strict reentrant winner and eventual return for every sufficiently large gain of the exact pinning eigenratio show failure of a natural monotone optimal-site ranking as feedback strength changes. It is an open-set property and a tiny exact regression test for numerical pin-placement algorithms, not merely a computed isolated equality or arbitrary scalar invariant. Its scope is a finite counterexample; no universal phase diagram or minimality is asserted.
